section.title: Where shipping rates come from
section.scenario: A checkout service quotes shipping for each order. The team signs a new carrier about once a month, and each carrier has its own rate rule.
section.question: Which piece fits this system better, and which stated fact decides it?
section.piece_a:
class ShippingQuote
  def initialize(carrier)
    @carrier = carrier
  end

  def cost_cents(order)
    case @carrier
    when "ups"   then UpsRate.new.cost_cents(order)
    when "fedex" then FedexRate.new.cost_cents(order)
    else raise KeyError, @carrier
    end
  end
end

answer_key.deciding_fact: A new carrier is added about once a month.
answer_key.principle: Open for extension, closed for modification: a new carrier should be a new rate class and one registry line, not an edit to working code.
answer_key.why_other_fails: Every new carrier means editing the case statement in cost_cents, so each monthly change touches code that already works for the other carriers.

answers.complete:
pick:b
The scenario says a new carrier arrives about once a month. With B, adding one is a new rate class plus one line in RATES, and cost_cents never changes, so it is open for extension and closed for modification. With A, every carrier means editing the case statement that already works for UPS and FedEx.
answers.partial:
pick:b
B is better, because the team signs a new carrier about once a month.
answers.miss:
pick:a
A is easier to read because all the carriers are listed in one method and there is no constant to look up, so a new teammate can follow it.

extra_answers.label: vague_correct_pick
extra_answers.answer:
pick:b
B looks cleaner and more professional, and it is the more modern way to write this kind of class.

extra_answers.label: other_pick_sound_reason
extra_answers.answer:
pick:a
The scenario says carriers are added monthly, so what matters is how cheap a new one is. A keeps every rule in one case statement, so a new carrier is one when line in one file, which I think is cheaper than adding a class and a registry entry.
